name: Thrust (NVIDIA CCCL)
listed_description: Parallel algorithms library with an STL-like interface for GPU vectors, reductions and sorting; now part of the CUDA Core Compute Libraries monorepo.
claim_text: Sorting 33,554,432 floats: GPU sort 17.76 ms, 44.17 ms with copies, against 2411.68 ms for single-threaded CPU STL sort.
book_benchmark: thrust::sort on device_vector of 33554432 floats against single-threaded std::sort on the host; host-to-device 12.95 ms and back 13.46 ms counted in the total; GPU model, compiler and flags not stated. The book notes the Thrust website chart compares against Intel TBB and leaves out transfer time.
guessed_baseline: std::sort (single-threaded); Intel oneTBB parallel sort on the vendor chart
found_in: book: GPU Programming with C++ and CUDA (2025), ch. 10, section Using Thrust to write GPU code

name: cuBLAS
listed_description: NVIDIA closed-source CUDA implementation of BLAS (matrix multiplication, vector operations); needs column-major data and a manual device copy.
claim_text: Order-1024 matrix multiplication: total GPU time 14.4 ms against 1404 ms on the single-threaded CPU, about 100 times faster.
book_benchmark: cublasSgemm plus cublasSgeam transpose on 1024x1024 float matrices against the book's own naive single-threaded CPU matmul; breakdown copy 0.89 ms, copy back 1.42 ms, compute 3.30 ms, handle overhead 8.79 ms; GPU model, compiler and flags not stated.
guessed_baseline: naive single-threaded CPU matrix multiplication; OpenBLAS or MKL would be the fair CPU baseline
found_in: book: GPU Programming with C++ and CUDA (2025), ch. 10, section Using cuBLAS to multiply matrices

name: Zero-copy NumPy buffer pointers into a CUDA library from Python
listed_description: Pass NumPy array data pointers (ctypes or a NumPy C-API extension) to a shared CUDA library, avoiding the per-element list copy of a plain CPython extension.
claim_text: Beyond 1M elements the list-copying wrapper cannot match direct data pointers; at 100,000 elements or fewer the simple wrapper wins.
book_benchmark: Figure 9.2 timing of a GPU vector-add call from Python, array sizes up to 10M int32, three variants (ctypes, list-copy extension, NumPy-pointer extension); mean of 10 runs after dropping lowest and highest; library built with a CMake debug profile; exact numbers only in the figure.
guessed_baseline: CPython C extension that copies each list element into a C array
found_in: book: GPU Programming with C++ and CUDA (2025), ch. 9, sections Passing numpy arrays to your library and Analyzing performance
